items.text: For a hero line or key number, use type.display. Don't use a brand-specific headline style. In the brand font for the product-page headline. Each brand speaks loudest in its product headline, on the shared scale.
For a section heading, use type.heading. Don't use bold body text. Headings stay one shared role; only the brand font changes.
For a supporting text, use type.caption. Don't use a brand-specific small style. One caption role serves fees, dates and hints in every brand.
For a title of a form page, use type.title. Don't use type.display. In the brand font. Sign-up and account pages share one title role in every brand.
For a parts of one item, use space.gap.tight. Don't use brand-specific spacing. Parts of one item sit close in every brand, so the shared parts look the same.
Between groups, use space.gap.group. Don't use brand-specific spacing. One group gap in every brand keeps sign-up forms the same shape.
Inside a button or input, use space.inset.control-x. Don't use brand-specific padding. Shared padding keeps buttons the same size in every brand.
Inside a card, panel or dialog, use space.inset.container. Don't use brand-specific padding. Cards hold offers the same way in every brand; only the corner and color change.
For an option in a menu or list, use radius.option. Don't use a hard-coded radius. (set by the brand). Each brand sets the option corner, and it nests inside that brand's menu corner.

For a something that grows past one line, use radius.element. Don't use radius.control. (set by the brand). A brand with pill controls would turn a text area into a capsule. The element corner stays sane in every brand.
For a corners of cards, menus and dialogs, use radius.surface. Don't use a hard-coded radius. (set by the brand). Each brand sets its own card corner; the role stays shared.
For a edges and dividers, use border-width.default. Don't use a brand-specific border width. One thin edge serves every brand. Color carries the brand, not line weight.

For the gap around a focus ring, use border-width.focus-offset and border-width.focus. Don't use a ring that touches the control. The gap sits around a ring of border-width.focus. The ring and its gap stay the same in every brand, so focus shows on any brand color.
For a panel opens, use motion.duration.panels. Don't use brand-specific motion. A relaxed open guides customers through sign-up the same way in every brand.
For the curve of any move, use motion.easing.standard. Don't use a brand-specific curve. One calm curve keeps the shared components the same in every brand.
For a hero or launch moment, use no hero motion. Don't use an intro animation for one brand. A brand-only animation would break the shared library.
For an icon beside text, use size.icon and icon.stroke-width. Don't use a brand-specific icon set. One icon set and size serve every brand; only the color changes.
For a most buttons and inputs, use size.control.default. Don't use size.control.compact. Customers sign up on phones, so every control fits a thumb in every brand.

For the main action on a screen, use size.control.large. Don't use a taller button for one brand. It is the same height as the default here. Brand color marks the main action. One height keeps every brand's forms the same.
For a button inside a field, use size.control.compact. Don't use size.control.default. A clear or show-password button fits inside the field in every brand.
For a control that is not available yet, use opacity.disabled. Don't use a grey color per brand. One fade level works on every brand color, so no brand needs its own disabled color.

items.text: For a number in a table, use type.body. Don't use a mono font. Prices sit in sentences and offers, not in columns to compare, so a mono font adds nothing in any brand.

For a button inside a field, use size.control.compact. Don't use size.control.default. A clear or show-password button fits inside the field in every brand.
Badge's warning tone isn't used. No plan or order state sits between running and failed; a coming renewal is news, not a warning.

items.text: For an error message, use color.status.danger and a sentence. Don't use the brand color. Status colors are shared, never branded.
For a delete or remove, use button secondary, then confirm with Button danger. Don't use button primary. Confirm before destroying data.

When no component in the inventory fits, use a component from the inventory with brand tokens. Don't use a component made for one brand. Brands change primitives, never components; one brand-only part breaks the shared library.
Button's secondary variant. The alternative that steps back, and the first step of a delete.
Button's danger variant. The confirm of a delete, the same red in every brand: danger never follows the brand.
Badge's danger tone. Card declined: the payment failed, so the plan will stop.
Alert's destructive variant. A billing problem such as a declined card: plain and specific, the same in every brand.

brand-q3.answer: Each brand brings its own face, on one shared scale
brand-q3.why: Each brand brings its own face, Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans or Poppins, on one shared type scale, so brands differ and the system stays one.

items.label: Readability
items.text: All three are screen sans faces with open shapes; the shared scale keeps body size and line height the same in every brand.

items.label: Legibility
items.text: Each brand checks its face's confusable characters in its own data; the scale gives every brand the same sizes to check at.

items.label: Scalability
items.text: All three have a wide range of weights, so every role in the shared scale has a weight in every brand.

items.label: Numerals
items.text: Inter has tabular figures; the brands that show tables lean on it.

items.label: Scripts and languages
items.text: Latin, with accents, in all three; Poppins also covers Devanagari. Other scripts need a face per brand.

items.label: Recognition
items.text: The face is how each brand is known on a shared system.

items.label: Familiarity
items.text: Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans and Poppins are widely seen on the web, so none feels strange.

items.label: Personality
items.text: A neutral base each brand can color: the face carries the brand, the scale stays neutral.

items.label: Performance
items.text: One family per brand: a page loads only its own brand's face.

items.label: Licensing
items.text: SIL Open Font License, all three: free to embed in apps and on the web.

items.label: Fallback and pairing
items.text: Each falls back to system-ui, as its tokens say; the shared scale keeps the layout steady while a face loads.

items.text: For a page title, use type.title in the brand font. Don't use a brand-specific style. Roles stay shared; only the brand font changes.
For a selected row or item, use color.surface.selected (from the brand). Don't use a fixed blue. Selection follows the brand color.
For a link, use color.text.link (from the brand). Don't use a fixed blue. Links take the brand's color, so they look native in each brand. A fixed blue would clash with some brands.
For the corners of buttons and inputs, use radius.control (set by the brand). Don't use a hard-coded radius. Each brand sets its own corner through the theme.
For the shape of a status badge, use radius.badge (set by the brand). Don't use a hard-coded shape. The brand sets the badge shape.
When someone switches to dark, use the dark mode of the active brand. Don't use one dark theme for all brands. Every brand ships light and dark.

For a value with no token, use the closest semantic token, then ask for a new one. Don't use a raw value or a brand primitive in the component. A raw value shows the same in every brand, so it breaks the theme.
For a corners of cards, menus and dialogs, use radius.surface. Don't use a hard-coded radius. (set by the brand). Each brand sets its own card corner; the role stays shared.
Sidebar's default variant. Account-area menu items, the same in every brand.
Sidebar's outline variant isn't used. Brands change color and corners, not the structure of the menu.
Empty's default variant isn't used. Shared structure in every brand: no brand pictures in empty states.
Item's muted variant. The current setting, with a soft fill from the brand.
Toggle's outline variant. A single toggle, with a border so it reads as a control in every brand.
